title: Guidance: retention of billing artifacts when customers request data erasure
text:
Guidance: retention of billing artifacts when customers request data erasure

["From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finchpayments.com>\\nTo: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai\\nCc: Procurement Team <procurement@finchpayments.com>\\nDate: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00\\nSubject: Billing records retention vs DSR — quick clarification\\n\\nHi Tessa,\\n\\nHope you're well — we're finalizing the security questionnaire and one item popped up from our finance team: if a user exercises a Data Subject Request (erasure) for their personal data, do you also purge the associated billing artifacts (usage logs, invoice lines, charge IDs), or do you retain them for accounting/audit reasons?\\n\\nFinch needs clarity because our compliance folks want to document the timeframe and any exceptions for invoices and usage ledgers tied to a user. If you have a short blurb or a point of contact who can confirm, that'd be very helpful.\\n\\nThanks,\\nLiam\\nProcurement Lead — Finch Payments\\nliam.oconnor@finchpayments.com\\n(415) 555-0194\\n\\n---\\nNote: attaching their procurement checklist in the next message if it helps.", 'From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai\\nTo: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai\\nDate: 2026-07-19T09:35:00-07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Billing records retention vs DSR — quick clarification\\n\\nTeam — forwarding a procurement question from Finch. They specifically ask whether we erase invoice/usage ledger items when a user requests erasure. High level: I think we retain billing artifacts for accounting/audit and legal reasons but need explicit language and any retention windows or exceptions we must surface. Can finance + legal confirm the official stance and a one-paragraph answer I can send back?\\n\\nPlease also flag any customer-facing wording we should avoid (e.g., \\"we never delete invoices\\") and any compliance links we can include.\\n\\nThanks — Tessa\\nHead of Sales Operations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\n[Forwarded message below]\\n\\n--- original ---\\nFrom: Liam O\'Connor <liam.oconnor@finchpayments.com>\\nTo: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai\\nDate: 2026-07-19T09:12:00-07:00\\nSubject: Billing records retention vs DSR — quick clarification', "From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai\\nTo: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai\\nCc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai\\nDate: 2026-07-19T11:02:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Billing records retention vs DSR — quick clarification\\n\\nTessa / Karthik — quick draft below for external consumption. Marissa: please add legal caveats.\\n\\nSuggested response for procurement:  \\n- Redwood retains billing artifacts (invoices, aggregated usage ledgers, charge IDs) for legitimate business needs including accounting, tax, and audit obligations.\\n- Per our retention schedule, invoice and ledger entries are retained for a minimum of 7 years to satisfy US accounting and tax recordkeeping requirements, unless a narrower timeframe is required by specific country-level laws.\\n- When a data erasure (DSR) is requested for a user profile, we will remove personal identifiers from operational product logs where feasible; however, we maintain a separate billing ledger and invoice records that are kept as necessary to meet financial and legal obligations. Any such ledger entries are treated as accounting records and are not typically considered part of the live profile data covered by user-facing erasure.\\n\\nQuick notes:  \\n- We should call out that we can pseudonymize or redact personal identifiers in billing entries on a case-by-case basis if requested and if it won't break accounting/audit trails.\\n- If Finch has a statutory requirement that conflicts with our standard retention schedule, we should route to legal for an exception assessment.\\n\\nI'll attach the summary and the retention matrix.\\n\\nNeha Kapoor\\nDirector, Finance Operations\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nAttachments: redwood_billing-data-retention-summary.pdf, dsr-exception-matrix.xlsx", 'From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai\\nTo: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai\\nDate: 2026-07-20T15:03:00-07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Billing records retention vs DSR — quick clarification\\n\\nThanks Neha — adding the legal framing (short):\\n\\n- Invoices and ledger entries constitute accounting records necessary for statutory reporting and anti-fraud controls; as such, they fall under a narrow exception to erasure obligations in many jurisdictions. We should state this clearly but avoid overpromising — e.g., say \\"we retain billing records as required by law and for legitimate accounting purposes\\" rather than an absolute timeframe in the customer-facing line.\\n- Recommended customer-facing paragraph (one-liner): \\"Redwood retains billing and invoicing records as necessary for accounting, tax, and audit obligations. Personal identifiers used solely for billing purposes may be redacted or pseudonymized where doing so does not conflict with legal or financial requirements; please contact your procurement or account team to discuss options.\\"\\n- If a customer requests full removal of invoice-level data tied to a specific charge, we need a documented legal/finance review to assess (a) statutory obligations, (b) downstream accounting impacts, and (c) whether an alternative (pseudonymization) satisfies the request.\\n\\nKarthik — can you confirm if we need to add any specifics for multi-tenant EU customers re: local VAT invoicing rules? Also flag any Marketplace/partner billing exceptions.\\n\\nMarissa Cole\\nSenior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\n---\\nMarissa attached a short guidance matrix (dsr-exception-matrix.xlsx) and the finance summary (redwood_billing-data-retention-summary.pdf).\\n\\n[End of thread]']
